title: AI Hands
shortDescription: A webcam hand-tracking sketch that turns finger distance into color.
longDescription: This browser sketch uses ml5.js hand-pose detection with p5.js to track the thumb and index fingertips. Their distance controls the red intensity of the canvas background, while blue circles mark both fingertips. The sketch hides the original camera element and displays a minimal visual response to the detected hand positions.
limitations: Requires camera access and a working hand-pose model; live tracking was not tested during catalog creation.

title: AI Hands Experiment 2
shortDescription: A hand-tracking experiment with fading finger trails and movement-triggered effects.
longDescription: This p5.js and ml5.js experiment draws a mirrored webcam view across the browser window and follows the first detected index fingertip. A fading trail records its path, while smoothed movement speed changes the size of the finger marker. Faster movements trigger an expanding impact ring. The source resets tracking coordinates after a resize and starts a new trail when a hand reappears.
limitations: Requires camera access and an externally loaded hand-pose library; live tracking was not tested during catalog creation.

title: Align Stretching Studio
shortDescription: A browser stretching prototype with 3D pose references and camera-based comparison.
longDescription: Align Stretching Studio presents 32 stretching and yoga movements with rotatable Three.js references and optional MediaPipe pose tracking. It compares detected joint angles with reference geometry, offers front and side inspection views, and includes a manual hold timer. The README describes local frame processing and a focus view that responds to stable tracking. This is a prototype: its 2D landmark comparisons estimate reference similarity and do not establish safe form or clinical correctness.
limitations: The README states that the prototype is not clinically validated and cannot assess pain, joint loading, balance, depth, or injury risk.
Camera angle, occlusion, and low-confidence landmarks can affect comparisons; live webcam behavior was not tested during catalog creation.

title: The Cloud Court

title: The Keeper of the Cloud Gate
shortDescription: An explorable Three.js guardian sculpture inspired by traditional Chinese paintings.
longDescription: This browser gallery presents a procedural celestial guardian with layered armor, a crown, staff, pearl, ribbons, and a lotus pedestal. Three.js orbit controls and five camera presets reveal the sculpture from different angles, while gallery, moonlit, and dawn lighting change its atmosphere. Visitors can toggle rotation, floating clouds, and wireframe, save a PNG view, or download a static GLB model. The project includes reference-inspired concept artwork and editable modeling source.
limitations: Requires WebGL 2 and a Vite development server or production build.
The exported GLB is static and excludes viewer lighting, controls, and atmosphere animation.
The visualization model includes double-sided ribbon surfaces and is not a watertight 3D-print file.

title: Circle Multiplication — Generative Study
shortDescription: A fullscreen p5.js artwork that evolves circular multiplication patterns automatically.
longDescription: This generative sketch places evenly spaced points around a circle and connects each point i to (i × m) mod N. Each page load randomizes the point count, initial multiplier, palette, and animation speed. As the multiplier increases, the straight chords form changing curve envelopes and woven patterns. The responsive canvas fills the viewport, and returning from a background tab resumes the composition without fast-forwarding.
limitations: The animation runs automatically; this minimal version has no on-screen controls.

title: Circle Multiplication — Interactive Math Garden
shortDescription: An interactive p5.js math garden for exploring multiplication patterns around a circle.
longDescription: This Chinese-language visualization connects each circle point i to (i × m) mod N, revealing cardioid-like envelopes, two-lobed curves, and woven patterns. Visitors can adjust the multiplier and point count, select three presets and four palettes, inspect individual connections near the circle, start or pause the animation, and export the canvas as a PNG. Explanatory text connects the geometric patterns to modular arithmetic, and the initial canvas remains still until animation is enabled.
limitations: Curve envelopes are finite chord approximations; the sketch draws straight connections.

title: Walker
shortDescription: A colorful random-walk sketch with fading paths and bounded motion.
longDescription: This p5.js sketch starts a walker at the center of the canvas and repeatedly draws short segments to randomly chosen nearby positions. Coordinates stay within the canvas, while gradually changing RGB values vary the path color. The program takes 120 steps per frame and overlays a translucent black background, leaving a fading record of the walk.
